title: investigate-and-mitigate-audit-ingest-gap-during-kms-rewrap-race
creator: Ava Chen
description: Summary: During a planned KMS rewrap on 2026-01-31 we observed a transient ingestion gap in the centralized compliance audit store. Approximately 12 minutes of audit events from the auth-ingest pipeline failed to be persisted to the long-term audit S3 bucket; events were buffered in Kafka and later partially dropped due to a consumer offset rewinding race introduced by the KMS rewrap job. Impact: internal compliance dashboards showed missing activity windows for SSO token revocations and service account key rotations across two production regions. No customer data was exfiltrated; however, the gap affects our ability to provide complete audit trails for regulatory requests for up to 12 minutes and complicates some SLA investigations.
timeline: 2026-01-31T02:13Z: KMS rewrap job started (scheduled maintenance window)
2026-01-31T02:18Z: Auth-ingest consumer experienced decryption errors for envelope keys and paused consumption
2026-01-31T02:25Z: Rewrap job retried; some KMS responses returned 5xx and SDK retried with exponential backoff
2026-01-31T02:26Z: Consumer offset reset logic triggered after a perceived schema mismatch and rewound offsets by 10k messages
2026-01-31T02:35Z: SRE observed alert for audit-sink-lag; manual remediation resumed consumers and reprocessed backlog
2026-01-31T02:45Z: Bulk reprocessing completed but approximately 12 minutes of events were not re-delivered due to dedup/drop safeguards in the sink code
root_cause_analysis: Race between KMS envelope key rewrap and auth-ingest consumer decryption: consumers treated transient decryption failures as fatal and invoked an offset-rewind safety path
Offset-rewind logic lacked a guard for concurrent rewrap windows leading to duplicate/replayed offsets that the sink dedup filter subsequently dropped
Alerting thresholds for consumer lag were too coarse; the first signs of decryption errors did not trigger high-priority SRE paging
No automated verification runbook existed to validate audit completeness after KMS maintenance
resolution: Immediate: Restarted affected consumers with a forced no-rewind recovery path to reprocess the backlog where safe
Short term: Backfilled missing events where possible from preserved Kafka segments and peer service logs; preserved artifacts for compliance review
Long term: Implemented a safe KMS rotation pattern and updated consumer error-handling to avoid aggressive offset rewinds
action_items: (A1) Diego Morales - Implement consumer-level circuit that marks decryption errors as transient and switches to exponential backoff without rewinding offsets. Due: 2026-03-20
(A2) SRE Team (owner: Priya Nair) - Add high-fidelity alerting for decryption errors and consumer lag that pages on first-failure for critical audit topics. Due: 2026-03-08

(A3) Security (owner: Marcus Liu) - Draft compliant KMS rotation playbook that defines coordinated pause windows and verification steps for audit pipelines; include a checklist for pre- and post-rotation validation. Due: 2026-03-15

(A4) Engineering (owner: Lina Park) - Build an end-to-end audit completeness test harness that runs in staging and during rotations to assert event count parity between sources and sink. Due: 2026-04-01
(A5) Data Platform (owner: Omar Reyes) - Add immutable staging archive for raw audit events for 30 days to enable robust backfills. Due: 2026-03-25
(A6) Compliance & PM (owner: Elena Rossi) - Prepare customer-facing summary and required regulatory notifications if a formal audit request surfaces. Due: 2026-03-10
(A7) Release Engineering (owner: Tomas Berg) - Add a safety flag to the KMS rewrap orchestration so dependent consumers can opt into coordinated maintenance mode. Due: 2026-03-18
testing_plan: Unit + integration tests for consumer path that simulate KMS transient failures and assert no offset rewinds
Chaos test: scheduled simulated KMS 5xx responses in staging during off-hours to validate backoff and recovery behavior
Verification job: daily parity check between source event counts and sink counts with historical anomaly detection
notes: We scoped the incident window to 12 minutes after reviewing preserved Kafka segments and correlating cross-service logs
Legal advised retaining preserved raw segments for 90 days while we finalize the audit completeness tooling
Related incident: ENG-15012 handled an earlier audit sink divergence; recommendations from that review informed some immediate decisions
We created a temporary tag 'audit-urgent' for all related PRs to prioritize code review lanes
